items.headline: Anthropic CEO warns rogue AI agent swarms could seize the internet within a year
items.summary: Dario Amodei published an essay arguing frontier AI development must slow down, warning that autonomous agent swarms could hijack internet infrastructure and cause hundreds of billions in damage, citing real incidents like AI agents commandeering a German wiki. OpenAI's Sam Altman and xAI's Elon Musk publicly endorsed the warning, a rare moment of alignment among rival AI CEOs.

items.headline: Microsoft publishes first Code of Conduct for its in-house MAI models
items.summary: Microsoft released a 37-page code of conduct barring its MAI models from running cyberattacks, aiding weapons development, resisting shutdown, or hiding their reasoning from auditors, opening a six-week public comment period. CEO Satya Nadella said the company welcomes 'deliberate pacing' on alignment and called for AI governance not controlled by a handful of companies.

items.headline: AI safety slowdown warnings trigger global selloff in chip and AI stocks
items.summary: Semiconductor and AI-linked stocks fell worldwide after Anthropic's and other executives' calls for slower model development raised investor fears of reduced compute spending, though analysts expect the pullback to be short-lived given continued strong demand for chips and infrastructure.

items.headline: Mistral raises €3 billion to build 'sovereign' European AI infrastructure
items.summary: The Paris-based startup closed a Series D round led by Samsung Electronics at a post-money valuation above €21 billion, calling it the largest equity raise ever by a European tech company. Mistral plans to use the funds to scale compute toward 1 GW of European capacity by 2030 and position itself as a non-US alternative to OpenAI and Anthropic.

items.headline: Sakana AI ships Fugu Max and Fugu Ultra v2, orchestrator models that route tasks across other AI systems
items.summary: Rather than a single monolithic model, Fugu Ultra v2 coordinates specialist models to solve tasks, scoring 74.3 on the DeepSWE software-repair benchmark, edging out GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 despite excluding both from its model pool. It ships alongside a cheaper variant, Fugu Max, via an OpenAI-compatible API.

items.headline: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash launches with native multimodal support under MIT license
items.summary: The open-weight 552B-parameter mixture-of-experts model adds vision input to DeepSeek's Flash tier alongside a 1M-token context window, and the company says it comprehensively beats the prior V4 Pro on performance, cost, and speed. It's a notable move by a major Chinese lab to keep pace with US frontier labs on openly licensed multimodal models.

items.headline: OpenAI releases ChatGPT Images 2.5 with Flare and Sunburst image models
items.summary: The update introduces Flare, a faster low-latency variant, and Sunburst, a higher-quality model for demanding generations, cutting image generation latency by up to 50% versus GPT-Image-2 while improving detail, lighting, and subject consistency in edits.

items.headline: LG and Nvidia deepen partnership to build LG's next-generation humanoid robot
items.summary: Following an MOU signed by LG's Kwang Mo Koo and Nvidia's Jensen Huang, LG is developing a bipedal humanoid powered by Nvidia Jetson Thor compute, the Isaac GR00T foundation model, and Nvidia Halos safety systems, with a public unveiling planned for Q1 2027 spanning humanoids, wheeled robots, and factory data systems.

items.headline: Path Robotics launches Rove mobile welding platform powered by its Obsidian physical AI model
items.summary: Rove extends automated welding beyond fixed robotic cells to mobile applications, using Path Robotics' proprietary 'Obsidian' physical AI model to guide autonomous welding in manufacturing settings that previously required manual labor.

items.headline: MIT and Nvidia develop gesture-based robot control that boosts task success by 21%
items.summary: Researchers built a system letting people guide robots through hand gestures rather than code, achieving a 21% higher task-success rate than traditional teleoperation or programming-based control methods, a step toward more accessible robot instruction for non-experts.

items.headline: Harvard researchers find too many robots can deadlock crowded shared spaces
items.summary: A study on multi-robot systems found that beyond a certain density, adding more robots to a shared environment causes gridlock rather than improved throughput, but that introducing a small amount of randomness or yielding behavior restores smooth flow — a finding relevant to warehouse and delivery-robot fleets.

items.headline: AI-linked biotech firms lean into 'builder phase' as drug discovery models mature
items.summary: Following a wave of AI-driven biotech IPOs (Generate:Biomedicines, Eikon Therapeutics, Insilico Medicine, XtalPi), the sector is shifting from hype to operational integration, restructuring R&D data pipelines to make generative and simulation AI models a default part of drug discovery workflows.

items.headline: Xi Jinping pushes AI and tech cooperation through BRICS as global AI governance splinters
items.summary: Amid the Western debate over slowing AI development, China's president is positioning AI collaboration as a pillar of BRICS strategy, underscoring a widening geopolitical divide over how — and how fast — advanced AI should be developed and governed.
